This release improves jewelry, metal and gem rendering.

#### Rendering

- Added the bloom property `highlightsOnly` (SS-10493). When enabled, only the light above `luminanceThreshold` blooms (soft knee of width `luminanceSmoothing`, per-pixel cap, tighter mipmap blur), so only highlights glow and bright metal keeps its colour. Unset `luminanceThreshold`, `luminanceSmoothing` and `mipmapBlur` then default to 1, 0.25 and true. With 8-bit buffers the threshold is capped at 0.8. Recommended together with `hdr` and Neutral tone mapping. Existing models and bloom without the property render unchanged.
- Added the bloom property `highlightLimit` (SS-10533, default 8). With `highlightsOnly` and `hdr`, it is the most bloom light a single pixel can add, in multiples of white. Very bright gems can leave a pale glow on the metal around them; a lower value (e.g. 1) removes it and keeps a small glow on the gems. Settings version 7.2 stores it; bloom without the property renders unchanged.
- Settings version 7.2 stores the new rendering options (SS-10497): `postprocessing.hdr`, the bloom properties `backgroundBloom` and `highlightsOnly`, `environment.mapPbrMode`, `environment.mapOrientation`, `material.physicalGemDispersion`, `material.gemTracing`, `material.gemNormalMapResolution`, and the HBAO/SSAO properties `mode` and `excludeGems`. Settings saved before 7.2 are converted with the old-look values, so existing models render unchanged.
- Added the HBAO and SSAO property `excludeGems` (SS-10497, default false). With `false`, gems are darkened by the composite ambient occlusion as before the gem exclusion of 3.23; set it to `true` to keep gems out of the ambient occlusion. The "shading" mode never darkens gems.
- Added the viewport property `physicalGemDispersion` (SS-10495, default false). When enabled, gem `refractionIndex` is the mid-spectrum (D line) value and `dispersion` is n(G line) − n(B line) (diamond 0.044); each colour channel uses its own refraction index when light enters, inside the stone and when it leaves, so blue bends most. Existing models keep the legacy dispersion, where `dispersion` offsets 1 / IOR by `dispersion * 0.025` per channel at entry only.
- Added the viewport properties `gemTracing` ("sphere" default, "facets") and `gemNormalMapResolution` (default 1024) (SS-10495). Facet-plane gem tracing and 512 px gem normal maps from 3.23 (SS-10470) are now opt-in; without them gems render as in 3.22. A gem material's `normalMapResolution` no longer defaults to 512; when unset the viewport value applies.
- Added the viewport properties `physicalGemFresnel` (default false) and `gemEnvironmentMapIntensity` (default 1) (SS-10532), stored in settings 7.2 as `material.physicalGemFresnel` and `material.gemEnvironmentMapIntensity`. With `physicalGemFresnel`, most light inside a gem leaves at the first facet it can pass (1 − Fresnel reflectance) instead of bouncing on, which gives larger, calmer facets like a real brilliant. `gemEnvironmentMapIntensity` scales the environment light of gems only, to match the stones to the scene for a given environment map. Existing models keep the legacy weights and the factor 1; the default settings use `physicalGemFresnel = true` and `gemEnvironmentMapIntensity = 1.2`.
- Added the viewport property `environmentMapOrientation` (SS-10522, "legacy" default, "threejs"). With "threejs", custom `.hdr` environment maps have the same orientation as in three.js and other tools; built-in presets render the same in both modes. Existing models keep the legacy orientation.
- New look for viewers without stored settings and for the settings presets (SS-10494). The default settings (`defaultSettings`, used by new models, by models without stored settings and by viewports created without settings) are now settings 7.2 with these values. Each one can be turned off with the option named in brackets:
    - `hdr` on (`postprocessing.hdr = false`), only in the `default`, `jewelry` and `furniture` presets; devices without half-float render targets keep 8-bit buffers. The presets without tone mapping (`medical`, `highPerformance`, `twoDimensional`) keep it off.
    - ambient occlusion leaves gems out (HBAO/SSAO `excludeGems = false`).
    - modern PBR environment shading (`environmentMapPbrMode = "legacy"`).
    - three.js orientation for custom `.hdr` maps (`environmentMapOrientation = "legacy"`).
    - physical gem dispersion (`physicalGemDispersion = false`), facet-plane gem tracing (`gemTracing = "sphere"`) and 512 px gem normal maps (`gemNormalMapResolution = 1024`).
    - physical Fresnel weights inside gems (`physicalGemFresnel = false`) and gem reflections at 1.2 (`gemEnvironmentMapIntensity = 1`).
- The `jewelry` preset additionally uses HBAO, a weak bloom on highlights only without background bloom (`highlightsOnly`, `backgroundBloom`, intensity 0.25), Neutral tone mapping with exposure 1.4, and SMAA on mobile instead of FXAA (SS-10494).
- Models with settings stored before 7.2 render unchanged. The engine defaults of all new options stay the old look.
